title: Valladolid debate
sides: Indigenous Americans are free by nature; convert without force
Some natives may be enslaved or subdued by war
summary: Spanish crown panel on the rights of Native Americans and the justice of conquest; no collective verdict was ever issued, and both sides claimed victory.
lines: in order to uproot crimes that offend nature

title: Oxford evolution debate (Huxley vs Wilberforce)
sides: T. H. Huxley / J. D. Hooker
summary: British Association meeting where the bishop and Darwin's defenders clashed; no verbatim record exists and the famous exchanges are reports.
lines: whether it was through his grandfather or his grandmother that he claimed his descent from a monkey
would not be ashamed to have a monkey for his ancestor

title: Lincoln-Douglas debate at Ottawa
sides: Opposed extending slavery into the territories
Popular sovereignty: settlers decide on slavery
summary: One of seven 1858 Illinois Senate-race debates on slavery in the territories and popular sovereignty.
lines: public sentiment is everything. With public sentiment, nothing can fail; without it, nothing can succeed
I believe this government cannot endure permanently half slave and half free (quoting Lincoln)

Popular sovereignty: settlers decide on slavery
summary: One of seven 1858 Illinois Senate-race debates on slavery in the territories and popular sovereignty.
lines: It is the eternal struggle between these two principles - right and wrong - throughout the world

title: Disputation of Barcelona
sides: Talmud shows the Messiah has come, and he is Jesus
The Messiah is human and has not yet come
summary: Before James I of Aragon, a Dominican convert and the great Jewish scholar debated the Messiah and true faith; the king rewarded Nachmanides yet he was later forced to leave Aragon.
lines: Why did they not convert and turn to the faith of Jesus, as Friar Paul did?
an unjust cause so nobly defended

title: Leipzig Debate
sides: Defended papal authority and Catholic teaching
summary: Eck debated Karlstadt on free will and then Luther on papal authority; it drove Luther to open break with Rome and threats of excommunication.

title: First Council of Nicaea
sides: The Son was created and subordinate to the Father
The Son is eternally begotten, of one substance with the Father
summary: Emperor Constantine's council condemned Arianism and issued a creed; Arius refused it and was exiled.
lines: of one substance with the Father
there was once when he was not

title: Trial of Socrates
sides: Socrates is guilty of impiety and corrupting the youth
Denied the charges and defended his philosophical mission
summary: A jury of about 501 voted 280 to 221 to convict Socrates, who was condemned to death by hemlock.
lines: The unexamined life is not worth living

title: Incoherence of the Philosophers vs Incoherence of the Incoherence
sides: Avicenna's school erred on seventeen points, three of them irreligious
Defended the philosophers against al-Ghazali's attack
summary: A written debate across a century: al-Ghazali's 1095 attack on philosophy was answered by Averroes in a dialogue quoting him point by point.

title: Religious debate at Karakorum
sides: Their own traditions; Möngke tolerated all faiths
summary: William of Rubruck attended debates among rival religions that the Mongols organized; Möngke said God gave men different ways as He gave the hand different fingers.
lines: Just as God gave different fingers to the hand so has He given different ways to men
We Mongols believe in one God, by Whom we live and die

title: The Great Debate (astronomy)
sides: Milky Way is the whole universe; ~300,000 light-years wide
Spiral nebulae are separate galaxies; Milky Way ~30,000 ly
summary: Shapley and Curtis argued the scale of the universe; Hubble's later work on Andromeda showed Curtis was right on the main point.

title: Bohr-Einstein debates
sides: Quantum mechanics is incomplete; locality must hold
summary: Einstein posed thought experiments (1927, light-box 1930, EPR 1935) and Bohr answered each, in a decade-long argument over quantum theory.
lines: I, at any rate, am convinced that He is not playing at dice
I don't understand precisely the point that Einstein is trying to make

title: Kitchen Debate
sides: Capitalism and consumer abundance serve the people
Communism will surpass the US; American gadgets are impractical
summary: Impromptu exchange in a model American kitchen at the American National Exhibition, broadcast across both countries.
lines: Don't you have a machine that puts food into the mouth and pushes it down?
What we want to do is make life more easy for our housewives

title: Putney Debates
sides: Keep the monarchy; vote only for property-owners
One man, one vote; freedom of conscience
summary: New Model Army officers and radicals argued over the constitution after the first civil war.
lines: the poorest hee that is in England hath a life to live, as the greatest hee

title: Webster-Hayne debate
sides: The Union is supreme; nullification is untenable
States may nullify federal laws such as the tariff
summary: Senate clash over tariffs and the nature of the Union, sparked by a land-survey resolution.
lines: Liberty and union, now and forever, one and inseparable

title: Council of Jerusalem
sides: Gentile converts need not be circumcised or keep the Mosaic Law
Gentiles must be circumcised and keep Moses' law
summary: Peter backed Paul and James proposed a compromise: the Apostolic Decree asked only abstention from idol-food, blood and sexual immorality.
lines: adding no further burden to you, except these necessary things

title: Council of Chalcedon
sides: One person in two natures, divine and human
Natures united without mixing or alteration
summary: About 520 bishops defined the person of Christ; the rejection led to a lasting schism with the Oriental Orthodox churches.
lines: perfect both in deity and in humanness

title: Diet of Worms
sides: Johann von Eck for Charles V
Will retract only what Scripture or reason refutes
summary: Luther refused to recant before the Emperor and was declared an outlaw; Wikiquote notes 'Here I stand' is not in the transcripts.
lines: I cannot and will not recant anything

title: Marburg Colloquy
sides: Christ's body is present in bread and wine
The bread is a sign; Christ is at the Father's right hand
summary: They agreed on 14 of 15 articles but not on the Eucharist, so Protestants stayed divided.
lines: Credere est edere (To believe is to eat)

title: Melian dialogue
sides: Neutral, appealed to justice and to Sparta
summary: Thucydides' dramatized negotiation before Athens besieged neutral Melos.
lines: the strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must

title: Samye debate (Council of Lhasa)
sides: Gradual path to enlightenment through analysis and merit
summary: Debate before King Trisong Detsen; Tibetan sources say Kamalashila won and Tibet followed the Indian tradition; Chinese sources dispute this.

title: Synod of Whitby
sides: Keep the Ionan Easter of Columba
summary: King Oswiu ruled for Rome, reasoning from Peter's keys; Northumbria joined the Roman Easter.
lines: Peter and Paul lived, taught, suffered, and are buried at Rome

title: Disputation of Tortosa
sides: Talmud proves the Messiah came; demanded it be burned
Profiat Duran, Yosef Albo and others
summary: Sixty-nine sessions before Antipope Benedict XIII; Aragon's Jewish community suffered mass conversions and loss of morale.

title: Disputation of Paris (Talmud trial)
sides: Talmud contains blasphemies and calls to harm gentiles
Talmud's 'Yeshu' is not Jesus; passages are hyperbole
summary: Led to the burning of 24 wagonloads of Hebrew manuscripts in 1242.
lines: not every Louis born in France is king

title: Ibadat Khana interfaith debates
sides: Their own faiths, courted by Akbar
summary: Akbar's Thursday evening discussions in his house of worship; he later created the Din-i-Ilahi.

title: Cuvier-Geoffroy debate
summary: Two-month Academy clash; Cuvier won in his time, Geoffroy's unity idea later influenced evolutionary thought.
lines: Can the organization of vertebrated animals be referred to one uniform type?

title: Leibniz-Clarke correspondence
sides: Relational space; Newtonianism harms natural theology
summary: Letters routed through Caroline of Ansbach about space, free will and the best of all possible worlds; ended with Leibniz's death.

title: Zhuangzi and Hui Shi on the joy of fish
sides: I know the fish are happy
You are not a fish; how can you know?
summary: Famous Zhuangzi exchange (ch. 17) on knowing another's experience.
lines: You're not a fish - how do you know what fish enjoy?
I know it by standing here beside the Hao

title: White Horse Dialogue
sides: A white horse is a horse
summary: Logical paradox from the Warring States: 'is not' as non-membership rather than identity.

title: Questions of King Milinda
summary: Indo-Greek king and monk in the Pali dialogue; Menander is said to have embraced Buddhism.

title: Shankara and Mandana Mishra
summary: Tradition holds Mandana became Shankara's disciple after a public debate; the Wikipedia article treats this as tradition.

title: Second Council of Nicaea
sides: Honor to an image passes to its prototype
summary: Restored icon veneration, reversed by a later iconoclast phase and finally in 843.
lines: the honor accorded to the image passes over to its prototype

title: Council of Ephesus
sides: Mary is Christotokos; stress the two natures
summary: The council condemned Nestorius, leading to the Nestorian schism.
lines: Anyone who dares to deny the Holy Virgin the title Theotokos is anathema

title: Buddhist-Taoist debate of 1258
place: Kaiping (Shangdu) area (location not stated in source)
summary: Kublai refuted the Taoists, converted 237 temples and destroyed copies of their texts.

title: Hillel and the convert
sides: Dismissed the request to teach the Torah on one foot
Gave the Golden Rule as the whole Torah
summary: Talmud Shabbat 31a: a would-be convert's challenge, answered by Hillel.
lines: What is hateful to you, do not do to your fellow: this is the whole Torah
